title: Remote state in Cloud Storage, locking and the lost-state accident

videos.script: Terraform remembers what it built in one file, the state. Lose it, and Terraform forgets everything it made. {{state}} On Google Cloud the state lives in a bucket. That bucket keeps every version, and lets almost nobody read it. {{bucket}} Two applies at once would overwrite each other. So Terraform takes a lock. Cloud Storage refuses the second writer, with a precondition. {{lock}} Then the accident. The state is deleted, and the next plan proposes to build everything again. {{accident}} You will find the right old version, and it will not be the newest one. Then you will put it back, and read the words no changes. {{restore}} And when no version survives, you will adopt real resources with an import. {{import}}
